what: KKR is an alternative asset manager. It raises money from pension funds and insurers, buys companies, infrastructure, property and credit with it, and earns management fees plus a share of the profits. It also owns the insurer Global Atlantic.
customers: Pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, insurers and wealthy individuals investing in its funds.
money: management fees, transaction fees and a share of investment profits
Global Atlantic annuities and the investment income on its assets
moat: A fifty-year record that lets it raise very large funds, with capital locked up for a decade, and relationships that give it first look at deals.
risks: Performance fees are lumpy and depend on selling investments at a profit
Higher interest rates make leveraged buyouts harder and exits slower
Private credit losses would hit both the funds and the insurance balance sheet
Reported earnings swing with the value it assigns to unsold investments
opportunities: Fee-paying assets under management keep rising, which is the steady part of earnings
Insurance provides permanent capital that does not have to be raised again
Individual investors are a large, barely tapped source of new money
watch: Fee-related earnings, the recurring part, rather than total reported profit.
